title: Cross-Border Data Mapping and Operator Guidance
body:
Purpose and audience:
This doc is an operator-focused, pragmatic playbook for mapping customer data flows to the regional controls we enforce at serving time. Target readers: on-call SREs, deployment operators for Private/Dedicated customers, and engineering leads who write routing/pinning policies. It complements the high-level residency strategy (confluence: Cross-Border Residency Overview) by translating policy into concrete operator actions, example routing configs, and trouble-shooting steps.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: user request routing, storage location decisions for transient artifacts (KV caches, logs, profiling), key management hints (KMS/HSM boundaries), and audit traces needed for compliance requests.
- Non-goal: full legal interpretation of residency laws (ask Legal or Compliance). This plays as an engineering-to-ops translation layer.

Guiding principles:
1) Minimal surface area: prefer routing rules that act on a single stable attribute (customer region tag, account residency) rather than brittle IP heuristics.
2) Fail-safe locality: when in doubt or when enforcement cannot be reliably determined, prefer the safer option (keep data in-county/region) and use explicit escalation for cross-region processing.
3) Observability-first: every routing decision must produce an audit log event with inputs + decision reason.
4) Explicit fallbacks: if a pinned region is unavailable, fallback must follow customer policy: fail-fast (reject), buffer & retry only if customer allows, or route to an approved secondary region.

Definitions & attributes we use for routing decisions:
- account_residency: authoritative field on customer account (set in control plane). Primary key for pinning.
- request_geo: inferred from request metadata (region header, client IP -> geo). Useful for routing defaults but NOT authoritative.
- model_variant_region: the regions where a model variant is provisioned (e.g., g4dn-us-east-1, ampere-eu-west-1).
- data_class: P0 (personal data with residency req), P1 (sensitive but no residency), P2 (non-sensitive/ephemeral).

Mapping matrix (operational summary) - read as: if account_residency=X and data_class=Y then action=Z:
- account_residency = EU, data_class = P0 -> route to eu-* model instances only; cache & temp files written to eu-managed storage; KMS key in EU.
- account_residency = US-CA, data_class = P0 -> route to us-west/us-east as allowed; do not route to non-US regions.
- account_residency not set, request_geo = JP, data_class = P0 -> create a temporary residency ticket for CS; default to jp region if model variant exists; otherwise ask for explicit consent.
- data_class = P2 (ephemeral) -> can use global pooling unless customer explicitly disallows.

Operator playbook: day-to-day tasks
1) Verifying account_residency mapping
   - Quick check: control plane UI (Accounts -> Residency) or API GET /accounts/{id} -> residency field.
   - If mismatch found (e.g., customer reports EU residency but control plane says US): open INFRA-2145 (example) and alert Customer Success to hold requests for any P0 traffic.

2) Inspecting routing decision for a given request
   - Use trace UI: search by request_id -> check routing.decision, routing.reason, model_variant_region, cached_prefix_hit.
   - CLI: redwoodctl trace get <request_id> --fields routing.* --output json
   - Expected fields: routing.decision (ALLOW_LOCAL / FALLBACK_APPROVED / REJECT), routing.reason (account_residency, missing_model_variant, outage_fallback), audit_event_id

3) Manual re-route for emergency maintenance
   - When performing region patching, set operator flag: operator.force_mode = maintenance and set maintenance_allowed_residencies = [list].
   - When forcing re-route for a specific account: POST /ops/reroute {account_id, target_region, reason, expires_at}. This creates an audit entry and a temporary override. Use only after CS approval.

Enforcement decision tree (operator quick-glance)
- Step A: Is account_residency present? yes -> go to Step B. no -> use request_geo fallback and flag for CS follow-up.
- Step B: Does model_variant_region include any region matching residency? yes -> select nearest matching region with capacity. no -> can we spin-up model_variant in residency region? if yes (autoscale_allowed) -> trigger deployment and queue request as PENDING; if no -> follow customer policy (reject or ask for consent).

Observable events (what to look for in logs)
- EVENT: residency.mismatch.detected -> created when request_geo != account_residency and data_class=P0.
- EVENT: routing.fallbackengaged -> includes fallback_reason, fallback_target_region, operator_override_id if used.
- EVENT: kms.cross-region-call -> only allowed for P2 or explicit approval.

Examples: routing config snippets (YAML-like, for operator reference)
# example 1: strict pinning for EU customers
- selector: account_residency == "EU"
  data_class: P0
  action: route
  allowed_regions: [eu-west-1, eu-central-1]
  fallback: reject
  kms_scope: eu
  audit_level: strict

# example 2: conservative fallback for enterprise pilot
- selector: account_residency == "APAC"
  data_class: P0
  action: route
  allowed_regions: [ap-northeast-1]
  fallback: route_to_approved_secondary
  approved_secondaries: [ap-southeast-1]
  operator_escalation: required

Common incidents and remedial steps
1) Incident: requests from EU accounts are routed to US model variants (detected via audit).
   - Probable causes: control-plane residency mapping rolled back in deployment, or a bug in selector evaluation.
   - Steps: check control plane current snapshot (GET /ops/snapshot/residency); confirm selectors deployed (GET /ops/selectors); if selector missing -> redeploy from repo ref infra/residency-selectors@main; run backfill to re-route queued requests if allowed.

2) Incident: model_variant not available in pinned region (capacity shortage).
   - Steps: check Dedicated pool capacity dashboards -> if pool exhausted, open capacity-bump runbook (link in linked_artifacts). If policy allows, engage approved_secondary. Otherwise set traffic to queued and notify CS.

Operator checklist (pre-maintenance)
- Verify no accounts with P0 traffic are pinned to the region you will take down.
- If there are, either schedule maintenance with those accounts or ensure approved_secondary is configured.
- Set maintenance window in control plane (ops.maintenance.create) with operator contact.
- Ensure audit retention for related events is extended to 1 year for compliance investigations.

Escalation and legal requests
- If Legal asks for a log of all routing decisions for an account over a period: run "redwoodctl audit query --account <id> --from <date> --to <date> --event routing.*" and produce the CSV. Route this to CS and Legal.
- For data subject access requests that include deletion of cached artifacts: follow deletion playbook (see linked_artifacts on Confluence) and ensure KMS key deletion is coordinated with Customer Success (KMS keys cannot be rotated without consent for P0).

Open questions / TODOs (working items)
- [TODO] Finish mapping for APAC sub-regions and legalese around cross-border analytics (assigned to Marcus).
- [Q] Should request_geo be promoted to authoritative when account_residency not set and request contains signed consent? (legal input required).
- [TODO] Add a lightweight UI for operators to preview the routing decision given a sample request payload. (design ticket INFRA-2278)

Appendix: quick commands
- redwoodctl account get <id> --fields residency
- redwoodctl ops reroute create --account <id> --region eu-west-1 --reason "maintenance" --expires 2025-02-01
- redwoodctl trace get <request_id> --fields routing.*,audit_event_id

Notes to self / informal: 
- Diego: re-check whether KMS audit records surface region for HSM-backed keys. If not, flag as gap.
- Hannah: we should add a small section for test customers where we allow global routing for P2 only.

References and links:

End of doc.
